growth_signal.note: confirmed by two sources in the run; the URLs were not saved
growth_signal.value: Annualised revenue surpassed £25.6m after sevenfold growth in a year, and it now operates in 35 US states.

entry.idea: Lawhive combines an online platform with a real regulated law firm so people and small businesses can get everyday legal help at a fixed, lower price than a high-street solicitor.
entry.lesson: Own the regulated part of an industry yourself instead of just selling software to it, and you can control price and quality together.
entry.name: Lawhive

growth.reason: Revenue grew sevenfold in a year, a very fast and clearly documented number.

market.reason: Everyday legal problems like family, property and employment issues affect a huge number of people and businesses across countries.

tech.reason: Owning a regulated law firm alongside the software is a real structural advantage, though the AI tools themselves could be matched by rivals.

sources.title: How Lawhive hit $55.8M revenue with a 199 person team

entry.twist: It uses AI tools to help its own lawyers handle more cases at once, so the savings come from efficiency, not from replacing lawyers with a chatbot.
entry.who_pays: Individuals and small businesses pay a fixed fee for family, divorce, property and employment legal work.
entry.why_now: People increasingly want legal help online instead of visiting a law office, and AI now helps lawyers work through routine cases much faster.
